To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liver of rats and pigs can be aerated by vascular perfusion with oxygen gas.

(1) the liver is a highly perfused and oxygenated organ, with a high metabolic demand; (2) the liver is vulnerable to ischemic injury, which can lead to organ failure; (3) the liver is susceptible to ischemia/reperfusion injury; (4) the liver is the most frequently transplanted organ; (5) the liver is highly susceptible to ischemia during transplantation, leading to a high incidence of posttransplant complications and death; (6)

(a) the use of gaseous oxygen as a persufflating gas is a safe and feasible method of aeration for the isolated perfused rat liver; and (b) the use of this method is associated with a reduction of the oxygen consumption of the liver and a reduction in the oxygen concentration of the effluent perfusate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biophysical aspects of liver oxygenation by vascular persufflations with gaseous O2.
the development of an innovative technology, vascular persufflation, for improving the oxygenation of the human body.
the biophysical aspects of liver oxygenation by means of vascular persufflation.

, based on the available data, the use of gaseous oxygen as a carrier gas in liver aeration by means of vascular persufflation (VPS) is safe and effective.
liver aeration with gaseous O2 by means of vascular persufflation can be performed with a high degree of safety and efficacy.
the results obtained in this study demonstrate that liver aeration is feasible, safe, and efficient.

the liver has a remarkable capacity for oxygenation.

the liver can be a viable target for oxygenation with vascular perfusion of gaseous oxygen (O2) in the absence of blood flow.
